podcast.body: This song from "The Joshua Tree" album was directly inspired by U2 roadie Greg Carroll, who was tragically killed in a motorcycle accident while working for the band. Bono's lyrics, inspired by a tour of Auckland with Carroll, combined with The Edge's guitar parts and contributions from three Toronto musicians at Grant Avenue Studios in Hamilton, brought the song to completion. "Both One Tree Hill and the Joshua Tree are dedicated to the memory of Rody Greg Carroll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Track 10 on the album, this emotional song is dedicated to Greg Carroll, a Maori man who was Bono's personal assistant and a beloved member of the band's crew. It commemorates Carroll's standout presence in Auckland and his untimely death. The vocal take used on the album was the only one Bono recorded, due to his intense grief. The song also critiques human rights atrocities in Chile under Augusto Pinochet and America's involvement, forming a trilogy with "Bullet the Blue Sky" and "Mothers of the Disappeared." It is rarely played in concert but is performed during special occasions and whenever the band plays in New Zealand. "It's a lovely, tidal, a lovely image, isn't it?"
